newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares held back by budget,rate uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares held back by budget,rate uncertainty.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased in early trade on Tuesday and traders said investor uncertainty over U.S. interest rate policy and Russian budget cuts would restrain the market's upward momentum in the next week or more.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index fell to 365.89 from a record 366.22 set on Monday.

"It's a very quiet market and very low volumes -- the general tendency is down," said Konstantin Melnikov, head of sales at Rinaco Plus, adding that second tier shares, many of which have taken off in the past few weeks, were sluggish.
Market leader national power utility UES edged down to $0.3110 from $0.3172 at 0900 GMT while regional power company Irkutskenergo ticked down to $0.283 from $0.287.
Traders said the market was taking a breather after its recent record-breaking performance and some said investors were wary ahead of a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday.

"A correction is likely after the last few days of rise and perhaps on some investor worries about the situation on the U.S. market," said Aton trader Boris Shvedsky. "I don't think there will be any (market) rise."
Economists are divided on whether key U.S. indicators of past weeks will prompt the Fed to raise interest rates.

Melnikov said the Fed decision would have only a passing influence on Russian shares and the market would head up again after fund managers had digested 1996 results currently being released by many companies.
Creditanstalt-Grant trader Andrei Galperin said this week's debate in the Russian parliament over proposed budget cuts, would influence the market more than U.S. interest rates.
"If the sequester gets resolved sucessfully then in two or three weeks the market could go up again," Galperin said.
